record.original_question: Let phi be a nonnegative integrable convolution kernel on R^d with integral 1, let phi_t(x) = t^{-d} phi(x/t), and define the convolution-type maximal operator by M_phi f(x) = sup_{t>0} (phi_t * |f|)(x). For a one-dimensional function f of bounded variation, does there always exist a finite constant C(phi) such that Var(M_phi f) <= C(phi) Var(f)? For which kernels phi can one prove the sharp constant C(phi) = 1?

evidence.quote: We define here the maximal operator of convolution type associated to ϕ by Mϕ f (x) = sup_{t>0} (ϕt ∗ |f|)(x).

Question 6. Let ϕ be a convolution kernel as described above, and let f : R → R be a function of bounded variation. Can we show that Var (Mϕ f) ≤ C Var (f) with C = C(ϕ)? For which ϕ can we actually show this with C = 1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\phi: \mathbb{R}^d \to [0,\infty)$ be a nonnegative integrable kernel with $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\phi(x)\,dx = 1$. For $t>0$ define the dilation $\phi_t(x) = t^{-d}\phi(x/t)$, and for a locally integrable $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ define the convolution-type maximal operator
$$M_\phi f(x) \;=\; \sup_{t>0}\,(\phi_t * |f|)(x), \qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^d.$$
Now restrict to $d=1$. For a function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ of bounded variation, let $\mathrm{Var}(f)$ denote its total variation on $\mathbb{R}$.

(a) Show that there exists a finite constant $C=C(\phi)$, depending only on $\phi$, such that
$$\mathrm{Var}(M_\phi f) \;\le\; C(\phi)\,\mathrm{Var}(f)$$
for every $f$ of bounded variation on $\mathbb{R}$.

(b) Characterize the class of kernels $\phi$ for which the sharp inequality
$$\mathrm{Var}(M_\phi f) \;\le\; \mathrm{Var}(f)$$
(i.e. $C(\phi)=1$) holds for all such $f$.
artifact.status_search_result: For specific kernels (heat kernel, Poisson kernel, and various smooth/log-concave radial kernels) the variation-diminishing property in dimension one with sharp constant C=1 is known. A general theorem covering arbitrary nonnegative integrable kernels with integral 1, and a complete characterization of those $\phi$ for which $C(\phi)=1$ holds, do not appear to be established; the question remains open in this generality.

status_evidence.title: On the variation of maximal operators of convolution type II
status_evidence.snippet: In dimension d=1 these maximal operators do not increase the L^p-variation of a function for any p>=1.
status_evidence.claim: Variation-diminishing property with sharp constant 1 is known for specific convolution kernels (heat, Poisson) in d=1.

status_evidence.title: On the variation of maximal operators of convolution type
status_evidence.snippet: Studies variation bounds for maximal operators associated to specific convolution kernels.
status_evidence.claim: Results are kernel-specific; a full characterization for general phi is not given.

status_evidence.title: Study of bounded variation on the H-L nontangential operator
status_evidence.snippet: For the nontangential maximal operator the constant C=1 in Var(M f) <= Var(f) is sharp.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp constant C=1 results are achieved in particular nontangential/convolution settings, supporting partial progress on (b).
